utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what is the name of the man who distributed these membership cards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can, his name was Bozo Bendzo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware that the SDS of Konjic was preparing and then in March 1992 actually adopted a decision on the formation of the Serb municipality of Konjic to which your village of Bjelovcina was to belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew very little about these things. I hardly knew anything, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, judging from the little that you did know, that other citizens of Konjic who were not Serbs, knew about this and who were severely opposed to such activities, believing that this would break up the municipality and that it was an anti-constitutional act?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My village was quite far removed from the town of Konjic, and I did not know anything about this, who was against and who was for this, and I was in the village at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, as you have already testified, at that time you were working at the Igman factory in Konjic, which is the most powerful, the most important factory in the municipality. It is mostly engaged in military production but you were working in the civilian department. I want to know whether you noticed among your colleagues from different ethnic groups, whether they were disturbed by these activities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that I was sent home to wait, and I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, please, Mr. Vukalo, is it true that with that aim in mind, which you said you knew very little about, the illegal arming of the Serb population started by the JNA through the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as the arming is concerned, I was living in this hamlet, Vukalo, which was about a kilometre away from the closest hamlet, and I do not know exactly what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, you know where Borci, Bjela and these places are in the eastern part of the Konjic municipality in the direction of Mount Prenj, on Mount Prenj actually?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I do from before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you probably know, Mr. Vukalo, that already in April a part of the Serb population from the city was moving in the direction of the Borci Lake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, I do not think anyone went from my village. As for other villages and the town, maybe they did, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you probably know that Kister and Borci were already under the control of the Serb forces already by then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of any Serb Army being there, nor do I know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Vukalo, that the other villages in which the Serbs constituted a majority were also being armed and that they had formed village guards on the main roads, interrupted traffic, allegedly defending themselves from attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My village, as I said, was surrounded by seven or eight and more, perhaps, Muslim villages. In the direction of the town there was the Croatian village of Pokojiste, and the majority Serb population was in the village of Bradina, so I do not know at all how this happened or what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, you were working in a military factory, Igman, and you must know that the arming of the Territorial Defence of the municipalities of Jablanica, Konjic and Borci were housed in the Ljuta area in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was working in the civilian section of the Igman factory and never in my life did I go into the military section of the factory. What there was there, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, before your testimony here today, and before you spoke to the authorised representative of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, did you also make a statement before the district court of Belgrade in October 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave a statement, I made a statement in Belgrade to this committee for the investigation of war crimes. I do not remember the person before whom I made this statement, and I also made a statement in the office of The Hague Tribunal in Belgrade, and that is all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, are you son of Spaso?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were born on 29th March 1964?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You say now, and you are aware of the fact that you are speaking under oath, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now you say that in October 1995 you did not make a statement to the district court in Belgrade on 22nd October 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave a statement to a man from this committee. That is how he introduced himself, from the committee, from Belgrade, as a court for the investigation of war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did this man who examined you introduce himself as Paunovic Miodrag, investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that he did -- yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did this judge, Mr. Vukalo, warn you that it was your duty to tell the truth and that you were not to withhold anything and that you were also warned of the consequences of perjury and that you had the duty to answer the questions put to you and that you were only not to answer those questions, in respect of yourself or a close relative of yours, which would inflict serious outrage upon you or a relative of yours, or entail material damage or a material prosecution for them; did the judge warn you of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me -- normally he asked me questions, and he asked me to tell him -- of course, he asked me to tell him the truth and I told him the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you signed every single page of what you had stated before that judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did sign something, probably that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Counsel, if I read a part of this statement, please be so kind as to tell me whether you had indeed stated this to the judge. On page 2: "In our quarters we Serbs are in the minority, but we relied upon the JNA and believed they would protect us. This belief was based on promises which the military commanders gave to Rajko Djordjic and other prominent Serbs in the area. The JNA, as far as I can recall, in April 1992, the JNA, as an armed force, withdrew from the region of Konjic, and Muslim forces took over the military facilities." Did you state this, Mr. Vukalo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the way it was formulated. Could you please be so kind, I apologise, as to repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "In this area, we Serbs are in the minority, but we relied on the JNA and we believed they would protect us. This belief was based on the promises made by the military commanders to Rajko Djordjic and other prominent Serbs in the area. As far as I can remember in April 1992 the JNA withdrew from the area of Konjic as an armed force."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This knowledge, only when I went out from the camp to be exchanged, actually I only heard then that some promises of that kind were being given to Rajko, but I do not know of it myself, whether that was actually the case, but when I left, when I left the camp, I heard that from some people down there in Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, please, on the basis of these facts which you presented to the judge as your own knowledge, do you know that the JNA as an armed force gave armaments through the SDS to the Serb population in the area of the municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That it gave arms to the Serb population, that the JNA gave arms to the Serb population is something I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have said before this Tribunal that in your village, there was no defence at all, there had been no preparations for a defence and that you had no arms; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I lived in my hamlet, in this hamlet where there were five or six households, all by the surname of Vukalo, and that as far as I knew there were very few men in the entire village, able bodied men, that is, and the village was surrounded by seven to eight Muslim villages, and the Croat village of Pokojiste was also in the surrounding belt and I was not aware of any organising actions for defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, in that statement when you were warned that it was your duty to tell the truth, just to remind you, I shall read a statement and please tell me whether it is true you stated this to the judge in Belgrade. Page 2, paragraph 2: "In order to protect ourselves and to preserve our lives, the lives of the members of our families and our property, we organised ourselves to defend ourselves with the few arms that we had. We maintained guard duty in order not to be suddenly attacked." Are these the words that you said under oath to the judge in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I arrived in Belgrade from the Serb republic, Republika Srpska, then I was tired. I had used all sorts of means of transportation to get there. Normally there was some hunting weapons in the village, some hunting rifles, and some people did have pistols, perhaps, but I do not know of it. I do not know who. There may have been some weapons, that is to say, I do not know how many. The people in the various hamlets which composed the village, we have these hamlets with five or ten households in each, with 500 metres or a kilometre dividing one from another.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But after you have explained this to us, now this means, Mr. Vukalo, that this morning when answering the questions of my distinguished colleague, the Prosecutor, in connection with whether there had been any defence and weapons and you replied in the negative, you were not exactly giving wholly the exact facts that you are aware of; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that in my hamlet there was no defence mounted at all, nor anything of the kind. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, if, before the investigating judge of the district court in Belgrade, before whom you also gave an account under oath, if then you said, "We did put up a resistance and the combat lasted for about an hour, but as we were outnumbered, we were defeated and we had to retreat and we moved in the surrounding forest until we were caught in the days after that together with the women and children", that certainly differs from what you have stated before this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When my village was attacked, when my hamlet was attacked, not a single bullet -- I did not hear a single bullet being fired from the direction of the houses in the hamlet in which I lived; nor did I hear any bullet fired from the village. Later, after I had already been locked up in Celebici, I found out that no one had been killed by the Croat or Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But I am asking you, Mr. Vukalo, I only read your words, the words you said in front of the investigative judge in Belgrade. I am not discussing the fact whether they are truthful or not, I just want to submit it to you that in this record which you have signed, you have said "we put up a resistance and the fight lasted for about an hour" and so on and so forth. Did you state this before that judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe it was formulated thus, but that is not what I said, that is for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the judge wrote this down although you did not say it in that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It may have been formulated thus, but that is certainly not what I stated. There was no resistance, and later I also found out in Celebici that no one had put up any resistance, even the people that did have the hunting rifles did not use them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, you have just now said that you were admitted to the SDS by Bendzo Dusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Bosko.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, thank you. Do you know Dusko Bendzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He lives at the far end, at the beginning, so to speak, of the village of Bjelovcina, and I am in the upper section, on the other end, but I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bjelovcina is not a very large village. How many inhabitants does it have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not too many, but the distances are great from hamlet to hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Strahinja Zivak, known as Strajo, from Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the man whose sons were executed in Bradina. Two of his sons were shot in Bradina, that is what I heard. Do you mean that man?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know, I am asking you whether you know this person. Do you know Strahinja Zivak who was the vice-president of the SDS in the municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have heard that two of his sons were executed down there in Bradina, and I may have seen him, but I cannot exactly say that I know him well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Vukalo, that Dusko Bendzo was entrusted, together with Strahinja Zivak, with arming the Serb population in the area of your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, is it true that the deputy of Dusko Bendzo was Slavoljub Bendzo, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Slavoljub Bendzo. I do not believe he engaged in any activities of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Miro Djurdjic and Mirco Babic, Mr. Vukalo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I know Miro Djurdjic and Mirco Babic, of course. They are from my village but from another hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that they had been charged with the task in the SDS, of which you just happened to be a member, to maintain contact, liaise with Strahinja Zivak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly. I cannot claim anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Vukalo, somewhere around the end of January, receive a call for the Reserve Corps of the JNA and towards the end of that year actually join the reserve corps in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hardly managed to serve the regular service in the JNA, because of cardiac surgery, which, of course, I have evidence of. I was operated on by Professor Isidor Papo, so that I was not capable -- I was not exactly militarily capable.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard that, Mr. Vukalo. You said so in connection with your service in the army of which you served the whole term, in fact. What I want to know is, did you respond to this call for entering the Reserve Corps in February in Mostar and then stay there perhaps for a couple of days, for the same reasons as you adduced here returned home; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vukalo, you have stated before this Tribunal that you did not have a rifle, that you were not armed, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not have a rifle of my own, no, I did not have a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it nevertheless true, Mr. Vukalo, that you were issued a machine gun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps someone who did that also wrote that, but I am not aware of any such fact myself. How these were issued, I am not aware that they were issued at all. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Vukalo, Amir Dzelilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He is from Kralupi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is from Kralupi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Vukalo, that you and your relative handed over, in Kralupi, machine guns to Amir Dzelilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came to Kralupi, some 100 metres away from the village, I was taking my mother, an old and sick woman, and my brother and a group with women and children from the hamlet, they were following us. We were not exactly all in one single group. I did not have any kind of weapon with me, on me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have said, Mr. Vukalo, that prior to this hearing you had been heard by the representative of the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand you exactly. Can you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1996, on 13th November, were you heard by a representative of the Prosecutor's office of the International Tribunal in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade, in the office of the Tribunal, of The Hague Tribunal, I gave a statement, yes. I do not remember the date. I expect it is written there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you told the truth to the best of your knowledge to that investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall exactly what I said to him. You can ask me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, at that time, Mr. Vukalo, sign a certificate after the statement had been translated to you, in which you said that you had given the statement of your own volition, that you were aware that it could be used in a procedure before this Tribunal, and that it was true and faithful to your recollection; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall having said exactly that, but I did sign something.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In order to refresh your memory in respect of what you told the investigator, I will read the following text, which is also contained in the statement: "I decided to try to surrender to the friends of my relative Vlado from Kralupi to Amir Dzelilovic, because the soldiers were shooting at random. Vlado, I went to seek him. Around 100 metres from Kralupi we surrendered to Amir and we also gave up the two rifles that we had kept to protect ourselves. In total, there were 20 of us who surrendered, including my mother." Did you say that to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The very expression as regards the expression "surrender", I have a problem with it. I was not fleeing with anyone. I approached Kralupi together with the women, children, the elderly, the sick, the infirm. We were scared because of the shooting and we tried to get away from it, in a way, and we approached our neighbours and wanted to approach our neighbours in the village of Kralupi to protect us, to give us shelter. We were beside ourselves with fear, we were surprised.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Kralupi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you and Vlado handed over, surrendered to Amir, his friend, two light machine guns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I was leading, taking my mother, old and infirm and sick, with my brother and that there was this staggered group of 20 of us, we were not all in a single group, and I gave him no weapons. I had none. In fact, I and my brother had to carry my mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if these words which I have just read to you are written down as your words, then the investigator wrote down something which you, in fact, did not say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe they did not understand, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to hear a translation of everything that you had said to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I spoke, I was having a very hard time, I was very embarrassed. At a certain point I really did not know exactly what I was saying. It is a very unpleasant memory for one to recall. I am trying to put it all behind, to forget it all, if that is at all a feasible proposition. I know that I had to stop every now and then because I could not endure it, to keep remembering those things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you do confirm that there is a difference between what I have read to you and that which you said in court here today; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I said here today and what you are reading, it may be formulated the way you read it, but I repeat that I had no weapons at all. Someone may have written that down the way it is written, but I do not know. I know that in Belgrade, in the office of the Tribunal of The Hague, I was shaken. I stopped, I interrupted my statement every now and then. I really had a hard time giving it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It would be time, your Honour, to adjourn today, for me to finish my cross-examination for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will continue tomorrow at 10.00 the cross-examination of this witness.

procedural_notes.text: (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
